Name: Event Extensions
Author: xzqute
Description:
[center] [img width=800]https://i.imgur.com/9FeE2OP.png[/img][/center]
[center][url=https://smapi.io][img]https://img.shields.io/badge/SMAPI-4.5.0+-brightgreen.svg[/img][/url] [img]https://img.shields.io/badge/Stardew%20Valley-1.6.15%20build%2024356-orange.svg[/img] [img]https://img.shields.io/badge/Version-1.0.0-blue.svg[/img][/center]
[center][size=4]Extra actors, parallel actions and scene controls for Stardew Valley event scripts.[/size][/center]

[heading][size=5][b]What it does[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4]Event Extensions adds 31 commands to ordinary Stardew Valley cutscenes. They let you create copies of NPCs and the player, change their appearance, give them dialogue, control the camera, stage local weather and lighting, and run timed effects in parallel.[/size]

[size=4]Add the commands to the usual slash-separated scripts in Data/Events/<LocationName>. Content Patcher packs can mix them with vanilla event commands. Event Extensions is independent of Event Studio and has no editor or project format of its own.[/size]

[size=4]Players only need Event Extensions when another mod depends on it. Installing the framework by itself adds no story events. The reference below gives event authors the syntax and a filled-in example for every command.[/size]

[heading][size=5][b]Requirements[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4]Event Extensions 1.0.0 requires Stardew Valley 1.6.15 build 24356 and SMAPI 4.5.0 or newer. It was tested on Windows with SMAPI 4.5.2. The game build is checked at startup: any other game file version disables command registration.[/size]

[heading][size=5][b]Installation[/b][/size][/heading]

[list]
[*][size=4]Install [/size][url=https://smapi.io][size=4]SMAPI[/size][/url][size=4] 4.5.0 or newer on the supported game build.[/size]
[*][size=4]Extract the framework ZIP into Stardew Valley/Mods. Keep EventExtensions.dll, EventExtensions.Core.dll and manifest.json together in the Event Extensions folder.[/size]
[*][size=4]Install the content mod that requires Event Extensions, then launch through SMAPI.[/size]
[/list] 

[size=4]Content Patcher is only needed for Content Patcher packs. Event Extensions itself does not require it and has no framework settings to configure.[/size]

 
[heading][size=5][b]For content pack authors[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4]Declare the framework as a required dependency in your pack's manifest.json:[/size]
 
[code]"Dependencies": [
    {
      "UniqueID": "xzqute.EventExtensions",
      "MinimumVersion": "1.0.0",
      "IsRequired": true
    }
  ][/code][size=4]If your pack already has a Dependencies array, add this entry to it. These commands belong inside event scripts, not the SMAPI console.[/size]

[size=4]Coordinates use tiles and include the event's tile offset. Clone positions and camera centers accept fractional tiles. Camera offsets and shake use world pixels. Durations use whole milliseconds; 0 applies the final state immediately. Use a decimal point for fractional numbers. Directions accept up, right, down and left, or 0, 1, 2 and 3. Easing defaults to linear; smoothstep is also available.[/size]

[size=4]Actor names are case-sensitive; command names are not. Actor and operation IDs are single words that start with a letter or underscore, followed by letters, digits, underscores or hyphens. IDs stay reserved for the whole event, even after removal or cancellation. Farmer aliases and spouse are reserved.[/size]

[size=4]Timed actions block the script until they finish unless you start them with async. Persistent facing, framing and installed effects do not block. A cameraFollow transition can block while it runs, but tracking stays active afterward.[/size]
 
[heading][size=5][b]Actors[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4][b]cloneActor[/b][/size]
[code]cloneActor <source> <id> <x> <y> <direction>[/code][size=4]Create an independent NPC or Farmer for the current event using the source's visible appearance. The copy gets its own ID and can be positioned, faded or changed separately. The source can be an actor already in the scene or an available NPC outside it.[/size]
 
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/vEiz67K.png[/img][/center]

[size=4][b]removeActor[/b][/size]
[code]removeActor <actor>[/code][size=4]Remove a presentation actor and cancel its active operations and tracking. Removing a borrowed Farmer only hides that actor for the scene; it does not delete the player. The removed ID stays reserved until the event ends.[/size]

[size=4][b]lookAt[/b][/size]
[code]lookAt <actor> <target|none> [enabled=true][/code][size=4]Keep an actor facing another actor as the target moves. Cardinal facing also updates during dialogue. Neither actor is moved. Use none or false to stop tracking and keep the last direction.[/size]
 
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/fZPpGtm.png[/img][/center]

[size=4][b]actorOpacity[/b][/size]
[code]actorOpacity <actor> <opacity> [durationMs=0] [ease][/code][size=4]Fade an actor's native body layers together. Opacity ranges from 0 to 1. Set a duration for a gradual fade, or leave it out to apply the value immediately. The shadow is rendered separately from the body.[/size]
 
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/T9AXzKB.png[/img][/center]

[size=4][b]actorMorph[/b][/size]
[code]actorMorph <actor> <source|reset>[/code][size=4]Change an actor's visible form to another actor or available NPC while keeping its ID, position and runtime role. NPC-to-Farmer and Farmer-to-NPC forms are supported. reset restores the original appearance. Morphing cancels managed animation; reset the morph before changing the original Farmer with farmerAppearance.[/size]

[heading][size=5][b]Farmer appearance[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4][b]farmerAppearance[/b][/size]
[code]farmerAppearance <actor> <property|copyFrom|reset> <arguments...>[/code][size=4]Change a Farmer's appearance for the scene. Clones keep independent clothing items. Existing players use a local render proxy, so their actual equipment and body settings stay unchanged. copyFrom copies another scene Farmer's visible appearance. reset restores all properties or only the named property.[/size]

  [size=4]Properties and values:[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4]body: male or female. skin: native index 0 to 23. hair: an index from the game's hairstyle catalog. accessory: native index, or none.[/size]
[*][size=4]hairColor, eyeColor, shirtColor and pantsColor: three RGB integers from 0 to 255. shirtColor requires a dyeable shirt.[/size]
[*][size=4]shirt and pants: clothing item IDs. hat and boots: item IDs, or none.[/size]
[*][size=4]bathingClothes and prismaticHair: true or false.[/size]
[/list]
[size=4]Qualified IDs such as (S)1000, (P)0, (H)0 and (B)504 are accepted, as are registered modded IDs of the matching type. copyFrom does not copy position, animation, inventory, rings or trinkets. Native texture replacements are supported; external appearance renderers need separate compatibility work.[/size]
 
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/4nWEt3q.png[/img][/center]

[heading][size=5][b]Dialogue[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4][b]actorName[/b][/size]
[code]actorName <actor> <name|reset>[/code][size=4]Set the display name used by speakAs. The actor's lookup ID and actual NPC or player name stay the same. Use reset to return to the current visual actor's default name. Native portrait settings determine whether the dialogue nameplate is shown.[/size]

[size=4][b]actorPortrait[/b][/size]
[code]actorPortrait <actor> <sourceActor|assetPath|none|reset>[/code][size=4]Set the portrait used by speakAs to another scene actor, an available NPC, a content asset or a PNG inside a mod folder. none removes the portrait. reset restores the current visual NPC's native portrait; Farmers have no native full portrait. PNG sheets must contain complete 64x64 portrait cells.[/size]

[size=4][b]speakAs[/b][/size]
[code]speakAs <actor> <textOrTranslationKey>[/code][size=4]Open native dialogue for any registered actor, including Farmer clones, and wait until the player closes it. Text can be literal dialogue or a native translation key, with normal dialogue formatting. It uses a separate presentation speaker and does not implicitly trigger vanilla speak social or quest notifications. Native action and question tokens still carry their normal effects.[/size]

[heading][size=5][b]Parallel actions and waits[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4][b]async[/b][/size]
[code]async <operationId> <command> <arguments...>[/code][size=4]Start a supported action under a unique operation ID and continue to the next command immediately. Independent channels can run together. Starting another action on the same channel cancels its predecessor. async also has controlled adapters for native animation and sound; it cannot run arbitrary vanilla or third-party commands.[/size]

[size=4]Supported actions: actorOpacity, cameraFollow, cameraPanTo, cameraPanBy, cameraOffset, cameraShake, musicFade, ambientLightFade, screenTint, letterbox, foreground and vignette. cameraFollow's transition can finish while continuous tracking stays active.[/size]
 
[code]async poseDemo animate Echo false false 300 0 1 2 3
async soundDemo playSound coin[/code][size=4]Animation arguments are actor, flip, loop, intervalMs, then frame indices. The interval must be a positive integer, and each frame must exist in the current visual sprite. Loops keep running until cancelled or replaced. Cancelling a managed sound stops that operation's own cue instance.[/size]

[size=4][b]wait[/b][/size]
[code]wait <operationId> [timeoutMs][/code][size=4]Wait until one named operation finishes, fails or is cancelled. The optional timeout is in milliseconds; 0 checks immediately. Reaching the end of a wait does not necessarily mean the operation completed successfully.[/size]
 
[size=4][b]waitAll[/b][/size]
[code]waitAll [timeoutMs][/code][size=4]Wait for all finite operations that are active when this command begins. Operations started later and persistent controllers do not extend the barrier. Target following, installed overlays and looped animations are not completion points for this wait.[/size]

[size=4][b]waitForActor[/b][/size]
[code]waitForActor <actor> [timeoutMs][/code][size=4]Wait until an actor's observed native movement finishes. This works with ordinary event movement; it does not start movement itself. Use a timeout when the scene needs a fixed upper limit.[/size]

[size=4][b]waitForAnimation[/b][/size]
[code]waitForAnimation <actor> [timeoutMs][/code][size=4]Wait for the actor's current finite visual animation. If no animation is active, the script continues immediately. Looped animations have no natural end and are rejected; cancel or stop them instead.[/size]

[size=4][b]waitForSound[/b][/size]
[code]waitForSound <cueName> [timeoutMs][/code][size=4]Wait for the tracked sound instances of the given cue name that are playing when this command starts. Later instances do not extend the wait. If none are playing, it continues immediately.[/size]

[size=4][b]cancel[/b][/size]
[code]cancel <operationId>[/code][size=4]Cancel a named operation. Its result stays available until the event ends. Use this to stop loops, interrupt a fade or stop a managed sound. Cancelling a transition does not automatically reset its installed visual state; use the corresponding command to restore that state.[/size]

[heading][size=5][b]Camera[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4][b]cameraFollow[/b][/size]
[code]cameraFollow <actor> [transitionMs=0] [ease][/code][size=4]Blend the camera to an actor's standing anchor, then keep following it. The transition blocks by default; tracking continues after it finishes. Use async for a transition that runs alongside other actions.[/size]

[size=4][b]cameraFrame[/b][/size]
[code]cameraFrame <actor1> <actor2> [actors...][/code][size=4]Keep the camera centered on the bounds of two or more distinct actors. It uses the midpoint between the outermost anchors and updates as actors move. It does not change zoom or guarantee that a group wider than the viewport will fit.[/size]

[size=4][b]cameraUnfollow[/b][/size]
[code]cameraUnfollow[/code][size=4]Stop continuous follow or framing while keeping the current framework camera position. cameraReset returns control to vanilla.[/size]

[size=4][b]cameraPanTo[/b][/size]
[code]cameraPanTo <x> <y> <durationMs> [ease][/code][size=4]Move the camera's base center to an absolute tile center, including the event tile offset. The pan replaces follow or framing. Map bounds can limit the final visible position.[/size]

[size=4][b]cameraPanBy[/b][/size]
[code]cameraPanBy <dx> <dy> <durationMs> [ease][/code][size=4]Move the camera's base center by a relative number of tiles. Pan replaces continuous follow or framing, while pixel offset and shake remain independent.[/size]

[size=4][b]cameraOffset[/b][/size]
[code]cameraOffset <xPx> <yPx> [durationMs=0] [ease][/code][size=4]Set a separate camera offset in world pixels, optionally fading from the current offset. Values are absolute offsets, not added increments. The offset can be combined with follow, framing or a pan. Set both values to 0 to clear it.[/size]

[size=4][b]cameraShake[/b][/size]
[code]cameraShake <amplitudePx> <durationMs> [frequencyHz=12][/code][size=4]Add a decaying camera oscillation without replacing the base movement or offset. Amplitude is in world pixels; frequency is in Hz, from 0 to 1000. The default frequency is 12 Hz.[/size]

[size=4][b]cameraReset[/b][/size]
[code]cameraReset[/code][size=4]Cancel framework camera operations and return camera control to the game. Follow, framing, offset and shake are released. Cleanup also releases camera ownership when the event ends.[/size]
[heading][size=5][b]Lighting and screen effects[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4][b]musicFade[/b][/size]
[code]musicFade <gain> <durationMs> [ease][/code][size=4]Multiply the user's current music volume by a gain from 0 to 1. Use 0 to mute and 1 to restore the user's volume. This command is available only on the main local screen, since split-screen music volume is shared.[/size]

[size=4][b]ambientLightFade[/b][/size]
[code]ambientLightFade <r> <g> <b> <durationMs> [ease][/code][size=4]Transition the native ambient darkness color using RGB values from 0 to 255. This controls the scene's lighting separately from a screen tint. It takes priority over automatic weather lighting until a native ambientLight command releases that ownership or sceneWeather reclaims it.[/size]

[size=4][b]letterbox[/b][/size]
[code]letterbox <heightFraction> [durationMs=0] [ease][/code][size=4]Add black bars at the top and bottom of the viewport. Each bar occupies the given fraction of the viewport height, from 0 to 0.5. Use 0 to remove them. cameraFrame accounts for the visible area between the bars when applying vertical map bounds.[/size]
 
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/ERtfZA4.png[/img][/center]

[size=4][b]foreground[/b][/size]
[code]foreground <texture|none> [opacity=1] [durationMs=0] [ease][/code][size=4]Stretch a temporary texture across the viewport in front of the world. It accepts a content asset or a PNG inside a mod folder, with opacity from 0 to 1 and an optional fade. none fades the current texture out and removes it. Foreground draws above tint and below vignette, black bars and dialogue.[/size]

[size=4]Mods/MyMod/overlay.png resolves a file inside a sibling mod folder or the game's Mods directory, falling back to a registered content asset. Paths outside Mods are rejected. File textures are cached for the event and released during cleanup; borrowed content textures are left to the game.[/size]
 
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/cLz4VjJ.png[/img][/center]

[size=4][b]vignette[/b][/size]
[code]vignette <strength> [radius=0.5] [softness=0.5] [durationMs=0] [ease][/code][size=4]Darken the screen edges independently of tint and foreground. Strength runs from 0 to 1. Radius, from 0 to 1, sets the clear inner area; softness, from 0.001 to 2, controls the width of the transition. Strength 0 clears the effect.[/size]
 
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/TEOs9Tl.png[/img][/center]

[heading][size=5][b]Scene weather and time[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4][b]sceneWeather[/b][/size]
[code]sceneWeather <current|clear|rain|storm|snow|wind|greenRain>[/code][size=4]Use native clear, rain, storm, snow, wind or greenRain weather for the event location on the current local screen. current restores the previous weather. Outdoor lighting follows native weather rules; indoor locations keep their shelter and lighting rules. Storm adds local flashes without causing farm lightning damage. Scene weather does not change tomorrow's forecast or publish its flags to shared world weather.[/size]

[size=4][b]sceneTime[/b][/size]
[code]sceneTime <HHMM|current>[/code][size=4]Set the local event clock and native time-dependent lighting. Time is HHMM, from 0600 through 2550, with minutes from 00 to 59. The selected time stays fixed during the event and persists across its map changes. current restores world time. It does not advance the world clock, run schedules, trigger day transitions or publish the staged time to the save or network.[/size]
 
[heading][size=5][b]Compatibility and limitations[/b][/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4]Use ordinary cutscenes. Festivals, weddings and playerControl scenes are rejected.[/size]
[*][size=4]Native content and item replacements are supported. Fashion Sense and other external appearance renderers require separate compatibility work. Specialized NPC subclasses must be cloned before opacity or morph composition; sprites larger than 256 source pixels per dimension are unsupported.[/size]
[*][size=4]Actor body composition stays inside the normal world draw order. Shadows, emotes and overhead effects keep their native role; actors are not lifted above dialogue or map AlwaysFront layers.[/size]
[*][size=4]Vanilla movement, animation, facing, viewport and ambient-light commands take back control from overlapping framework features. Account for this when mixing them with persistent controllers.[/size]
[*][size=4]After changeLocation, clone IDs and appearance remain, but spatial operations stop and clones are hidden until placed again. NPC clones can use native warp. Recreate named Farmer clones on the new map using a new ID.[/size]
[*][size=4]Tint, bars, foreground, vignette, local weather/time and music gain persist across maps within the same event. Completion, skipping and cleanup release the framework's temporary scene state and owned resources.[/size]
[*][size=4]Vanilla rewards, inventory, friendship, quests, flags and exit warps keep their native behavior. Calling ordinary NPC dialogue or native action tokens can still have the game's usual side effects.[/size]
[*][size=4]There is no combat system, HUD toggle, actor scaling, camera zoom or public C# extension API in this version.[/size]
[*][size=4]If another mod has already registered any of the same command names or aliases, Event Extensions leaves those handlers alone and does not register its own versions.[/size]
[/list]
[heading][size=5][b]Waits and errors[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4]Operations can finish as Completed, Cancelled or Failed. Their results remain available until cleanup. By default, known finite operations have their remaining duration plus five seconds to finish. External movement, animation and sound waits use a 30-second watchdog. You can supply a different timeout. A timeout advances the script and records a diagnostic; it does not forcibly stop the action or destroy borrowed resources.[/size]

[size=4]Invalid arguments and missing IDs are reported and skipped so the event can continue. Diagnostics use SMAPI Trace logging. A successful startup does not print a command-registration message.[/size]

[heading][size=5][b]Performance[/b][/size][/heading]
[size=4]Runtime work stays on the main thread. Actor composition targets are reused, file-backed textures are cached for the event, and vignette uses a reusable 128x128 mask that is uploaded when its parameters change. Rendering more composed actors at once still costs more. The current automated measurements are fixture checks, not a whole-game FPS benchmark.[/size]

[heading][size=5][b]Troubleshooting[/b][/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4]Commands unavailable? Check the exact game build, the two DLLs and manifest, required dependencies, and command-name conflicts in the SMAPI log.[/size]
[*][size=4]A camera pan seems smaller than expected? Check map bounds, viewport size and active camera commands. Small maps may leave little room for movement.[/size]
[*][size=4]Weather or time does not change the lighting? Try an outdoor location and check whether ambientLight or ambientLightFade is overriding automatic lighting.[/size]
[*][size=4]A portrait or foreground fails to load? Check the asset path or file inside Mods. Portrait PNGs also need complete 64x64 cells.[/size]
[*][size=4]Reporting a bug? Include your SMAPI log, the complete event entry and key, installed versions, other event/appearance mods, and whether you were playing alone, as host, as farmhand or in split-screen.[/size]
[/list]
